source.title: Qdrant Vector Store: search filter leaks across nodes and is lost after the first retrieve-as-tool call

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
# Issue body (English, self-filed bug report)

## Problem

The Qdrant Vector Store node stores the node's **Search Filter** option in a class-level static field: `ExtendedQdrantVectorStore.defaultFilter` in `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/vector_store/VectorStoreQdrant/VectorStoreQdrant.node.ts`.

That static is the only way the filter reaches the retriever path: `handleRetrieveOperation` (retrieve mode) returns the raw store, the Vector Store Retriever node wraps it with `vectorStore.asRetriever(topK)`, and LangChain's `VectorStoreRetriever` then calls `similaritySearch(query, k)` without a filter — the n8n `similaritySearch` override merges in `ExtendedQdrantVectorStore.defaultFilter`.

Because the field is `static`, **every** `ExtendedQdrantVectorStore.fromExistingCollection(...)` call overwrites it for **all** instances in the worker process.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a workflow with two Qdrant Vector Store nodes in **Retrieve** mode, both pointing at the same collection, with different `Search Filter` JSON, e.g. node A filters `metadata.tenant = a`, node B filters `metadata.tenant = b`.
2. Connect each node to its own Vector Store Retriever + AI Agent.
3. Initialize/execute both store nodes (any order), then ask agent A something that triggers retrieval.

A second, even easier trigger: any Qdrant node in **Retrieve as Tool** mode. That mode builds a fresh client on **every tool call** with `filter = undefined` (see `retrieveAsToolOperation.ts`), which resets the static to `{}` — so any earlier Qdrant retriever loses its filter entirely after the agent uses the tool.

## Expected behavior

Each Qdrant Vector Store instance searches with its own configured filter.

## Actual behavior

- Whichever Qdrant store is constructed **last** decides the filter for every other Qdrant store in the process: agent A retrieves agent B's documents (wrong tenant's data), or
- the filter silently disappears (`{}`) when the last construction had no filter.

On queue-mode workers the process is shared across concurrent executions, so the stale filter can also leak across executions, not just across nodes in one workflow.

## Root cause

`defaultFilter` is declared `private static` and assigned in the static `fromExistingCollection`; `similaritySearch` reads the same single shared slot:

```ts
private static defaultFilter: IDataObject = {};

static async fromExistingCollection(embeddings, args, defaultFilter: IDataObject = {}) {
	ExtendedQdrantVectorStore.defaultFilter = defaultFilter;
	return await super.fromExistingCollection(embeddings, args);
}

async similaritySearch(query, k, filter?, callbacks?) {
	const mergedFilter = { ...ExtendedQdrantVectorStore.defaultFilter, ...filter };
	return await super.similaritySearch(query, k, mergedFilter, callbacks);
}
```

`@langchain/qdrant`'s `fromExistingCollection` builds the store with `new this(...)`, so the returned object is an `ExtendedQdrantVectorStore` instance — the filter can be kept per instance instead (assign it to the instance after construction and merge `this.defaultFilter` in `similaritySearch`).

## n8n version

Present on current `master` (`fd889ba`).

comments.text: One detail about the retrieve-as-tool path: it constructs the fresh client with `filter` set to `undefined`, then passes the tool’s filter to `similaritySearchVectorWithScore` for that call. With the current static assignment, the construction can therefore replace another store’s default filter with `{}`; the tool’s own per-call filter is still supplied. Keeping the default on each store instance would avoid that cross-store overwrite.
